meta.storyTitle: Isolate reviewer access and fetch dependency advisories

summary.prose: This Story checks a repository's dependencies against public advisories. The reviewer runs with the SAME host access as the controller itself -- no sandboxing or egress/filesystem restriction is attempted, since constraining the reviewer would degrade the review's own accuracy (explicit user direction, applied across the Epic). s2 instead focuses on two things that matter for correctness regardless of access level: pointing each package manager's audit at the repository's own actual dependencies (never an ambient or mismatched environment pip-audit/govulncheck would otherwise default to), and computing one deterministic content identity by hashing the complete set of required input files' actual bytes directly, so s3 can verify it reviewed the exact same content. Every destination a manager's audit actually reaches, and what it discloses there, is recorded for the final report's audit trail -- observability, not an enforced boundary. A manager, dependency or source that cannot be correctly targeted or resolved is reported as an explicit gap, never silently skipped and never run against the wrong target.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: The Epic adds a standalone orchestration module (outside src/workflow/review-round/) that owns model selection, dependency-advisory collection, code-assessment execution, and reporting, and supplies review-round's existing RoundDriverHooks.security hook as a thin adapter. review-round itself stays unchanged except for the one call site invoking that hook; the data shapes it already exports (SecurityFinding, SecurityLocator, EvidenceProvider, VerificationReceipt) are populated, never redefined.

ownedContracts.name: SecurityAdvisoryEvidence
ownedContracts.purpose: Carries s2's dependency-advisory collection outcome (controller-side, no model) across the boundary: the pinned contentIdentity it was collected against (so s3 can verify it recomputes/matches the same identity before trusting this evidence), the queried coordinates, the actual advisory matches with affected versions and provenance, the per-match advisory destination actually reached (recorded for audit, not enforced -- s2 runs with controller-equivalent access, no sandboxing), the per-manager input mode used (manifest-scoped | isolated-environment | confined-source-copy | unsupported, retained as a correctness/targeting concern, not an isolation one), and the dependencies/sources that stayed unresolved, unavailable or unsupported -- so s3 can report confirmed affected dependencies and unverified coverage as DISTINCT values bound to the SAME content identity as its own code findings.

boundary.internal: pkg_audit's package-manager resolution; s2 runs with the SAME host access as the controller itself -- no network or filesystem sandboxing is attempted (explicit user direction: constraining the reviewer degrades review accuracy). s2 instead RECORDS, per manager, which destination was actually reached and what was disclosed (observability for the final report, not a basis for refusal); the documented per-manager input/mode mapping (npm/pnpm/yarn/cargo: manifest+lockfile scope; pip/pipenv/poetry: the repository's own resolved environment, never the ambient active environment pip-audit defaults to; go: the repository's own module source directly, since govulncheck performs source-level analysis, not a manifest read) is retained as a CORRECTNESS/targeting requirement, with an explicit coverage gap for any manager s2 cannot correctly target under that mapping; and the advisory-match collection that populates SecurityAdvisoryEvidence (stamped with the pinned contentIdentity, computed by hashing the complete required input set's actual bytes directly) stay private to s2. No model, tool-loop, or CLI session is involved in s2 at all. ac2's gap-reporting distinguishes a SUCCESSFUL audit that found vulnerabilities (a valid, parseable result regardless of exit code -- pkg_audit's own auditArgv already marks every supported manager nonZeroOk:true) from an EXECUTION GAP (spawn failure, unparseable output, an unsupported manager, or a manager s2's input/mode mapping cannot correctly target) -- these are never conflated.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Model-tier resolution (extending src/config/role-taxonomy.ts with a security role), availability/credential checks, and the no-silent-fallback blocker-reporting logic stay private to s1; only the resolved SecurityModelSelection crosses its boundary. s1 must also specify the configuration contract for an INDEPENDENTLY selectable security-model binding (distinct from core/mid/cheap) and its interaction with coreFloor enforcement and unavailable-model handling; this is s1's central, still-open design question.

The RoundDriverHooks.security adapter function; the CliProvider.runReadOnlySession dispatch of the code-vulnerability pass against the SAME pinned contentIdentity s2 collected against (recomputed/verified by s3, refusing on a content MISMATCH only -- never on an access/enforcement question), using s1's resolved model, with the SAME host access every other CLI-backed session in this codebase already has (no additional credential/out-of-scope/MCP denial gate; explicit user direction, applied across the Epic's design). The call into runReviewRound and the separate ownership of everything runReviewRound itself does NOT do (sandbox/mutation checkpoint execution, round reconciliation, VerificationReceipt persistence, and checkpoint cleanup); the mapping from the review's pinned contentIdentity onto the epicHash/storyId identity persistVerificationReceipt requires; and the assembly of SecurityFinding/SecurityEvidence plus a supplemental report structure stay private to s3. It consumes s1's SecurityModelSelection and s2's SecurityAdvisoryEvidence to produce that report.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase A -- foundational contracts (model selection and dependency-advisory collection)

nonFunctional.security: s2 and s3 run with the SAME host access as the controller itself (explicit user direction: sandboxing or constraining the reviewer degrades the review's own accuracy, applied across this Epic's design) -- neither attempts network or filesystem confinement, and this codebase has no sandbox/network-namespace infrastructure to build such confinement on in any case. s2 records, per manager, which destination was actually reached and what was disclosed, attaching that to SecurityAdvisoryEvidence for audit; this is observability, not an enforced boundary, and is NOT a basis for refusing to run a manager. s2's per-manager input/mode mapping (manifest-scoped for npm/pnpm/yarn/cargo; the repository's own resolved environment for pip/pipenv/poetry, since pip-audit otherwise audits the ambient active environment; the repository's own module source for go, since govulncheck performs source-level analysis) is retained as a CORRECTNESS requirement -- pointing each tool at the right target -- not an isolation one; a manager outside that mapping is still an explicit coverage gap, because s2 cannot correctly target it, not because it cannot be confined. s3's code-vulnerability pass is dispatched through CliProvider.runReadOnlySession with the same access level every other CLI-backed session in this codebase already has; no additional credential/out-of-scope/MCP denial or negative-access test gates dispatch. contentIdentity remains a hard, non-negotiable CORRECTNESS invariant, unrelated to the access-level decision: s2 and s3 must operate against the exact same pinned content, computed by hashing the complete, required input set's actual bytes directly (never inferred from git status alone, which can miss a tracked file marked assume-unchanged) -- s3 recomputes and verifies this identity before trusting s2's evidence, refusing ONLY on an actual content mismatch.
nonFunctional.observability: Every checkpoint run -- pass or fail, whether or not a SecurityFinding corroborates it -- is recorded as a VerificationReceipt (already built, src/workflow/review-round/receipt-record.ts), so a security review's execution is auditable independent of its findings. s3 owns stamping that record with the epicHash/storyId persistVerificationReceipt requires, mapped from the review's own pinned contentIdentity. s2's per-manager recorded destinations/disclosures (see nonFunctional.security) are the equivalent audit trail for the dependency-advisory pass.
nonFunctional.durability: No new persistent storage is introduced for s1/s2's own outputs (SecurityModelSelection, SecurityAdvisoryEvidence are transient per-review values); the durable records are the already-typed SecurityFinding/VerificationReceipt heads the shared round-driver machinery (Epic 03f4fd3b9102aab8) persists, plus s3's new supplemental report structure (not yet a stored artifact type; its persistence mechanism is an open question for the s3 LLD).
nonFunctional.performance: Not a stated constraint for this Epic; the new module's cost is bounded by one pkg_audit invocation (per targeted manager) and one CLI read-only session per request, not a new background job.

api.name: computeContentIdentity
api.signature: function computeContentIdentity(repoPath: string, targets: ReviewTargets): Promise<string>

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: The registered repo root git_rev_parse runs against, and the base every targets.entries path is resolved and validated against -- removes the ambiguity of a relative path across two registered repos.

parameters.name: targets
parameters.purpose: The round's submitter-owned content list (artifact-core/types.ts:345-347); computeContentIdentity expands each manager's COMPLETE required input set (see requiredInputsForManager) around these entries, not just the single path named.

returns.meaning: A deterministic digest over the repo's HEAD commit sha (via git_rev_parse) plus a sha256 (Node's own crypto, not git_hash_object) of EVERY required input file's actual, current raw bytes -- read and hashed unconditionally, never gated on whether git status reports a file as dirty/untracked. This closes the gap where a tracked file marked assume-unchanged diverges from HEAD while git status stays empty: computeContentIdentity still sees the real, current bytes because it reads every required file directly rather than trusting git's own change-tracking to decide what to include. s3 recomputes the same function independently against the same repoPath/targets to verify it reviewed the same content.

errors.condition: the target repository's git state cannot be read (not a git repository, repoPath not registered, or the underlying git_rev_parse call fails)
a targets.entries path resolves outside repoPath

preconditions: repoPath is a registered repo root with a resolvable HEAD
postconditions: pure function of the repo's current file bytes, repoPath and targets.entries -- calling it twice with no intervening change to the complete per-manager input set yields the identical string
never includes file content from outside repoPath or the complete per-manager input set

hashes raw file bytes directly (crypto.createHash('sha256') over the file read from disk) -- never delegates to git_hash_object, which applies git attribute clean filters before hashing and can collide on different raw content
never relies on git status/dirty-file enumeration to decide which files to hash -- every required input file is read and hashed unconditionally

api.name: collectDependencyAdvisories
api.signature: function collectDependencyAdvisories(repoPath: string, targets: ReviewTargets): Promise<SecurityAdvisoryEvidence>

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: Same registered repo root as computeContentIdentity; also the root enumerateManagers walks to find every manifest in scope.

parameters.name: targets
parameters.purpose: Bounds which manifests/managers are in scope for this collection, same as computeContentIdentity's targets.

returns.meaning: sc2's full result: contentIdentity (via computeContentIdentity), queriedCoordinates, matches, perManagerMode, unresolvedDependencies, and unavailableSources.

preconditions: enumerateManagers(repoPath, targets) has found at least an attempt-worthy manifest, or the result is an all-gaps SecurityAdvisoryEvidence
postconditions: every manager it attempts runs with the SAME host access as the controller itself -- no sandboxing, no isolated copy; pkg_audit runs directly against repoPath (or the manager's own manifest directory within it), the real environment

every manager is correctly TARGETED per requiredInputsForManager's mapping (the repository's own resolved environment for pip/pipenv/poetry, the repository's own module source for go) -- never left pointed at an ambient or mismatched default; a manager s2 cannot correctly target produces an explicit coverage gap (perManagerMode 'unsupported'), never a mis-targeted run

records, per manager, the destination actually reached and what was disclosed there, attached to the returned SecurityAdvisoryEvidence for audit -- this is observability, never a basis for refusing to run a manager
every queried coordinate ends up in exactly one of matches or unresolvedDependencies (or contributes to a 'no findings' result) -- never silently dropped
the returned contentIdentity equals computeContentIdentity(repoPath, targets) computed over the exact same repository state each manager actually audited
never throws -- every manager-level failure becomes an explicit perManagerMode/unavailableSources/unresolvedDependencies entry, not an exception, matching ac2's 'remain explicit gaps' requirement

api.name: createDependencySbomEvidenceProvider

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: Captured in the returned provider's closure and forwarded to collectDependencyAdvisories on every run() call, since EvidenceProvider.run's own fixed signature (evidence-provider.ts:26-40) carries no repo-identity field.

returns.meaning: An object with category:'dependency-sbom' whose run(input) calls collectDependencyAdvisories(repoPath, input.targets) and maps its matches into the thin EvidenceProviderOutput.evidence (one SecurityEvidence per match, providerCategory:'dependency-sbom', locator pointing at the matched coordinate's manifest file). The richer SecurityAdvisoryEvidence itself is NOT part of this return value -- the orchestration module obtains sc2 directly by calling collectDependencyAdvisories, not through the registry.

postconditions: the returned object satisfies the EvidenceProvider interface exactly (evidence-provider.ts:26-40), so the existing EvidenceProviderRegistry can hold it under the 'dependency-sbom' key unchanged

dataModelChanges.entity: pkgAuditTool execute -- plain pip pointed at the repository's own requirements, never the ambient environment
dataModelChanges.details: CURRENT INVARIANT BEING REPLACED: auditArgv's pip case runs `['pip-audit', '-f', 'json']` (pkg/index.ts:164-175) with no `-r`/`--path` argument, so pip-audit audits whatever is installed in the ambient active Python environment by default -- not the repository's own requirements file, even though cwd points at it. NEW behavior: when a requirements file (requirements.txt, or one generated from Pipfile.lock/poetry.lock for pipenv/poetry) is present, auditArgv's pip/pipenv/poetry cases pass it explicitly via pip-audit's own `-r <path>` argument, so the audit targets the repository's own declared dependencies directly. This is a correctness/targeting fix, not an isolation one -- resolution and installation behave exactly as pip-audit's own documented `-r` mode already does; no `--no-deps`/`--require-hashes` restriction is imposed, since the reviewer runs with controller-equivalent access and a full, accurate resolution is preferred over a restricted one.

dataModelChanges.entity: Repository-root threading (repoPath) through computeContentIdentity, collectDependencyAdvisories, createDependencySbomEvidenceProvider
dataModelChanges.details: ReviewTargets carries no repository identity (entries are bare paths -- artifact-core/types.ts:345-347), so a relative path like package.json is ambiguous across two registered repos sharing that relative path. Every s2-owned function now takes an explicit repoPath (a registered repo root); every targets.entries path is validated as resolving inside repoPath before use, and git_rev_parse and the manifest enumerator both run with repoPath as their base, never the daemon's own ambient process.cwd().

requiredInputsForManager(manager) names the manifest (and, where one exists, the lockfile) that manager's audit actually needs, used only to point pkg_audit's existing `cwd` at the right real directory and, for pip/pipenv/poetry, to resolve the right `-r <requirements path>` argument (generating one from Pipfile.lock/poetry.lock when the native manager has no bare requirements.txt). There is no copying, no temp directory, and no isolation step -- s2 runs pkg_audit directly against the manager's real manifest location within repoPath, matching the controller's own access level.

dataModelChanges.entity: Per-manager destination/disclosure recording (replaces the revision-2 destination pin + negative-access verification)
dataModelChanges.details: After each manager's audit completes, s2 records which destination that manager's native tool actually reached (e.g. the configured registry/index/advisory-database host) and a short description of what was disclosed there, attaching both to the corresponding SecurityAdvisoryMatch.advisoryDestination and the final report. This is pure observability -- no proxy, no destination pin, no negative-access probe, and no refusal based on network behavior; s2 runs with the same host access as the controller and trusts the same native tool behavior the controller would.

dataModelChanges.entity: enumerateManagers (replaces reliance on detectManager's single-match precedence)
dataModelChanges.details: detectManager(cwd) (pkg/index.ts) returns only the FIRST manager it finds via a fixed lockfile precedence order, stopping at the first match -- it never enumerates co-located managers (e.g. a Python requirements.txt beside an npm package.json in the same directory) or nested project directories. enumerateManagers(repoPath, targets) instead walks every manifest/lockfile signal within repoPath bounded by targets.entries' own directories, producing one {manager, manifestDir} pair per manifest found; two different managers' manifests in two different directories are each audited independently, while two conflicting manifests in the SAME directory for the SAME manager family are flagged as an unresolved ambiguity rather than guessed at.

Translates each manager's own result shape (npm/pnpm's parsed JSON, pip-audit's JSON, cargo audit's JSON; yarn/go's non-JSON text output, since auditArgv marks them expectsJson:false) into the common SecurityAdvisoryMatch[] shape (coordinate, advisoryId, affectedVersions, severity, provenance, advisoryDestination). An unparseable or malformed result is recorded in unavailableSources as an execution gap, never silently treated as 'no findings' -- distinct from a successful audit that legitimately found nothing.

The HLD-defined output record this Story owns, produced by collectDependencyAdvisories exactly as the HLD's interfaceSketch specifies: { contentIdentity, readOnly: true, queriedCoordinates, matches: SecurityAdvisoryMatch[], perManagerMode, unresolvedDependencies, unavailableSources }. Lives in the Epic's new standalone orchestration module (outside src/workflow/review-round/), and crosses the s2->s3 boundary unchanged.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: collectDependencyAdvisories is the sole producer of SecurityAdvisoryEvidence. For every manager enumerateManagers finds, it stamps the result with computeContentIdentity (hashing the complete required input set's actual bytes directly), correctly targets that manager's audit at the repository's own real manifest/environment/source (never an ambient default), runs pkg_audit with the same host access the controller has, records the destination actually reached and what was disclosed, and maps the output into SecurityAdvisoryMatch[]. Every unresolved/unavailable/unsupported case is recorded explicitly rather than dropped. s3 consumes the returned value directly (not through the EvidenceProvider registry) to recompute and verify contentIdentity before trusting the evidence, and to report confirmed affected dependencies vs. unverified coverage as distinct values in its own report.

errorCases.scenario: A targets.entries path resolves outside repoPath (e.g. a path-traversal or a mismatched relative path against the wrong registered repo).
errorCases.detection: computeContentIdentity/collectDependencyAdvisories validate every targets.entries path against repoPath before use.
errorCases.response: Throws (computeContentIdentity) / records an explicit gap for that entry (collectDependencyAdvisories); the out-of-scope path is never read.
errorCases.userImpact: A misconfigured or ambiguous path never silently includes the wrong repository's content.

errorCases.scenario: pkg_audit's underlying CLI binary is not installed for a manager enumerateManagers found (e.g. pip-audit itself is missing).
errorCases.detection: runShell's existing r.spawnError flag (pkg/index.ts:487-489's existing check) surfaces back to collectDependencyAdvisories.
errorCases.response: That manager is recorded in unavailableSources as an execution gap, never conflated with 'no findings reported'.
errorCases.userImpact: Distinguishes 'the audit tool is genuinely absent' from 'the audit ran and found nothing.'

errorCases.scenario: A manager's audit output is unparseable or malformed in a way distinct from pkg_audit's normal nonZeroOk:true 'findings reported' convention (e.g. expectsJson:true but JSON.parse fails, or an unexpected text shape for a non-JSON manager).
errorCases.detection: The per-manager raw-output-to-SecurityAdvisoryMatch mapper fails to extract any usable fields from r.stdout.
errorCases.response: Recorded in unavailableSources as an execution gap; never silently reported as a clean, findings-free result.
errorCases.userImpact: A parse failure never masquerades as a successful security check.

errorCases.scenario: A plain `pip` project has neither a requirements.txt nor a Pipfile.lock/poetry.lock -- there is nothing to point pip-audit's `-r` argument at.
errorCases.detection: requiredInputsForManager finds no requirements-shaped file for the detected pip project.
errorCases.response: Recorded as perManagerMode 'unsupported' (an explicit coverage gap) -- never falls back to auditing the ambient active environment.
errorCases.userImpact: Never silently reverts to the wrong (ambient) target just because the expected file is missing.

errorCases.scenario: Two different package-manager manifests for the SAME manager family are found in the same directory under repoPath (e.g. two conflicting lockfiles enumerateManagers cannot disambiguate).
errorCases.detection: enumerateManagers detects more than one candidate manifest for the same manager family in one directory.
errorCases.response: That directory's manager is recorded as an unresolved ambiguity (added to unresolvedDependencies with a note), never guessed at by picking one arbitrarily.
errorCases.userImpact: Never silently audits the wrong lockfile when two plausible ones exist.

edgeCases.input: A manager's audit legitimately exits non-zero with a fully parseable 'findings reported' result (pkg_audit's own existing nonZeroOk:true convention for every manager).
edgeCases.expected: Treated as a SUCCESSFUL audit -- matches populated from the parsed result, NOT an execution gap, preserving ac2's own distinction and pkg_audit's existing behavior unchanged.

edgeCases.input: No manifest for a given manager is present anywhere under repoPath within targets.entries' directories (that manager simply is not used by this repo).
edgeCases.expected: That manager is never attempted and its absence is not reported as an unavailableSource or unresolvedDependency -- correctly out of scope, not a gap.

edgeCases.input: The same coordinate name happens to appear via two different managers in two different directories in the same review.
edgeCases.expected: Each manager's match is recorded independently in matches, keyed by its own manager-scoped coordinate; no de-duplication that could hide one manager's distinct finding.

edgeCases.input: A tracked requirements/lockfile is marked assume-unchanged (git update-index --assume-unchanged) and its real on-disk content has diverged from HEAD; git status reports nothing.
edgeCases.expected: computeContentIdentity still reflects the change, because it reads and hashes every required input file's actual current bytes directly -- it never consults git status/dirty-file enumeration to decide what to include.

edgeCases.input: A required input file has git attributes that would apply a clean filter (e.g. line-ending normalization) if hashed via git_hash_object.
edgeCases.expected: computeContentIdentity hashes the file's raw bytes directly via Node's crypto, bypassing git attribute filters entirely, so the digest reflects exactly what pkg_audit actually reads -- never a filter-transformed value.

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test (node --test) with node:assert, matching the daemon tools convention this Story's own pkg_audit change sits beside (e.g. src/daemon/tools/__tests__/approval-broker.test.ts's `import test from 'node:test'` pattern).

testLevels.purpose: Prove computeContentIdentity's determinism, scoping, and unconditional raw-byte hashing in isolation, with a fake git-plumbing layer for git_rev_parse and real Node crypto + real filesystem fixtures for the file-hashing step.
subjects: computeContentIdentity: identical HEAD sha + identical required-input-set bytes -> identical string on repeated calls
computeContentIdentity: a change to a required input file's raw bytes -> a different string, even when the file is marked assume-unchanged (git status reports nothing)
computeContentIdentity: a change to a file OUTSIDE the required input set -> no change to the string
computeContentIdentity: a targets.entries path resolving outside repoPath -> throws
computeContentIdentity: a file with git attributes that would apply a clean filter -> the digest reflects the RAW bytes, not the filtered content
computeContentIdentity: git state unreadable (not a git repo) -> throws the documented Error

testLevels.purpose: Prove enumerateManagers finds every manifest signal, not just the first lockfile-precedence match, and flags same-directory ambiguity.
subjects: enumerateManagers: a directory with both an npm package.json and a Python requirements.txt -> two independent {manager, manifestDir} entries, not one
enumerateManagers: two conflicting lockfiles for the same manager family in one directory -> flagged as an unresolved ambiguity, never silently picking one
enumerateManagers: no manifest anywhere under repoPath -> an empty result, no gap reported for any manager

testLevels.purpose: Prove collectDependencyAdvisories' per-manager targeting, destination recording, and gap-reporting logic in isolation, with a fake pkg_audit invocation -- no real subprocesses.
subjects: collectDependencyAdvisories: pkg_audit spawnError for a manager -> recorded in unavailableSources, not conflated with 'no findings'
collectDependencyAdvisories: a non-zero exit with parseable output (pkg_audit's nonZeroOk:true convention) -> treated as a successful audit, matches populated, no gap
collectDependencyAdvisories: unparseable/malformed output -> recorded in unavailableSources, never reported as 'no findings'
collectDependencyAdvisories: a plain pip project with no requirements.txt/lockfile -> perManagerMode 'unsupported', never falls back to the ambient environment
collectDependencyAdvisories: pip-audit is invoked with `-r <requirements path>` pointed at the repository's own file, not the ambient environment
collectDependencyAdvisories: the destination each manager's audit actually reached is recorded on the corresponding SecurityAdvisoryMatch.advisoryDestination
collectDependencyAdvisories: the same coordinate name via two different managers in two different directories -> two independent matches, no de-duplication
fixturesNeeded: a fake pkg_audit invocation (controllable exit code / stdout / spawnError per manager) standing in for the real pkgAuditTool.execute call

repoPath fixtures with varying manifest combinations (npm+pip in separate dirs, go-only, no manifest, duplicate coordinate names across managers, Pipfile.lock/poetry.lock fixtures for the -r path generation)

testLevels.purpose: Prove createDependencySbomEvidenceProvider's registry-contract mapping -- the thin EvidenceProviderOutput must stay distinct from the richer SecurityAdvisoryEvidence.
subjects: createDependencySbomEvidenceProvider(repoPath).category === 'dependency-sbom'

createDependencySbomEvidenceProvider(repoPath).run(input) maps each SecurityAdvisoryMatch into one SecurityEvidence with providerCategory:'dependency-sbom' and a locator pointing at the matched coordinate's manifest file

the EvidenceProviderOutput never carries advisoryId/affectedVersions/severity/provenance/advisoryDestination directly -- those stay in the richer SecurityAdvisoryEvidence obtained separately via collectDependencyAdvisories

testLevels.purpose: Prove pip-audit's `-r` targeting actually audits the repository's own requirements rather than the ambient environment end-to-end, against a real subprocess -- gated behind INSRC_LIVE_TESTS=1 per the project's existing live-service-test convention.

alternativesConsidered.name: Minimal additive pkg_audit env override + per-call ephemeral allowlisting proxy
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add one optional `env` field to pkgAuditTool's existing inputSchema (cwd is already there), forwarded to runShell's own per-call env option; s2's orchestration module starts a short-lived allowlisting proxy and per-manager scoped cwd/env for exactly the duration of one audit call.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Extend pkgAuditTool's inputSchema/execute with the pip/pipenv/poetry `-r <requirements path>` fix (an additive-at-the-call-site change, not a schema addition) -- the single code change to pkg_audit itself, directly satisfying ac2's 'not a new fetcher' requirement. s2's own module: (1) computes contentIdentity by hashing the complete required input set's actual bytes directly; (2) enumerates every manager in scope and points pkg_audit's existing `cwd` (and, for pip-family managers, `-r`) at the repository's own real manifest/requirements, never an isolated copy or an ambient default; (3) runs pkg_audit with the same host access the controller has -- no proxy, no sandbox, no negative-access probe; (4) records the destination each manager's audit actually reached for the final report; (5) maps pkg_audit's raw per-manager output into SecurityAdvisoryMatch[], and (6) wraps the result into both the thin EvidenceProviderOutput (for the dependency-sbom registry contract) and the richer SecurityAdvisoryEvidence (sc2, returned directly for s3). Revision 3 drops the revision-2 proxy/negative-access-probe/isolated-materialization machinery entirely, per the HLD's own revision-5 amendment (the reviewer runs with controller-equivalent access, not sandboxed); the choice of a1 over a2/a3 stands unchanged -- a1 remains the smallest change that reuses pkg_audit directly.
pros: Reuses pkg_audit directly -- the only code change is pointing pip-family managers at the repo's own requirements via -r, satisfying ac2's 'not a new fetcher' requirement
No proxy, isolation, or verification machinery to build or maintain -- the reviewer runs with the same host access as the controller, per the HLD's revision-5 policy
Full, accurate resolution (no --no-deps/--require-hashes restriction) is preferred over a restricted one now that sandboxing is explicitly out of scope
cons: s2's own reports of which destination each manager reached are self-reported by the native tool, not independently verified -- an accepted, documented tradeoff (HLD risky bit 'Controller-equivalent access tradeoff'), not a gap this Story tries to close

alternativesConsidered.name: A wholly separate scoped-audit fetcher bypassing pkg_audit
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Build a new, standalone dependency-advisory fetcher that duplicates argv-building and subprocess invocation for each manager itself, instead of calling pkgAuditTool at all.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Write a new module that re-implements per-manager argv construction (duplicating auditArgv's logic, which is module-private and not exported from pkg/index.ts) and calls runShell directly with full control over cwd/env/proxy from the start, never touching pkgAuditTool's existing execute() path.
pros: Total control over every invocation detail from the first line, no coordination with pkg_audit's existing input/output shape at all
cons: Directly violates ac2's explicit text: 'implemented as the EvidenceProvider registry's dependency-sbom category wired to the existing pkg_audit tool ..., not a new fetcher' -- this alternative IS a new fetcher
Duplicates per-manager argv logic (auditArgv) that already exists and is already correct, doubling the maintenance surface for npm/pnpm/yarn/pip/pipenv/poetry/go/cargo argument shapes
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates ac2's explicit text outright by being exactly the 'new fetcher' the Story forbids, and duplicates auditArgv's already-correct per-manager logic -- rejected regardless of its other merits.

alternativesConsidered.name: Mutate the daemon's own process.env around the pkg_audit call
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Avoid changing pkg_audit's code at all by temporarily overwriting process.env.HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY (and restoring it afterward) for the duration of the call, since pkgAuditTool.execute defaults to process.env when no env override is passed.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Before calling pkgAuditTool.execute, set process.env.HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY to the ephemeral proxy's address and the manager's scoped settings; restore the prior values in a finally block after the call returns.
pros: Zero changes to pkg_audit's own source at all
cons: process.env is GLOBAL to the daemon's Node process, which the daemon's own threaded/session architecture runs concurrent, unrelated shell-backed tool calls inside (per the project's daemon.threads design) -- a security review's proxy env could leak onto, or be clobbered by, a completely unrelated concurrent shell call in the same process, a correctness and isolation hazard a1's per-call options.env entirely avoids

A restore-in-finally still has a window where a concurrent call on another async task sees the mutated environment, since Node's single-threaded event loop interleaves awaits -- this is not a theoretical risk given the daemon already runs many concurrent tool calls per session
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Nominally keeps ac2's wiring intact (same pkgAuditTool.execute call site, no schema change) but the enforcement mechanism itself is unsafe under the daemon's own concurrent, threaded session model -- a global process.env mutation is not a boundary sc2's 'enforced, not merely observed' advisoryDestination can rely on. Moot at revision 3 since no env-based network enforcement of any kind is attempted anymore, but a1's per-call scoping remains the better code-change pattern regardless.
